sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Sarath
 Writ Petition No.809 of 2024
Order:

Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, the learned Government Pleader for Irrigation Department, appearing for the respondent No.1, the learned Government Pleader for Finance and Planning for the respondent No.2 and the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for the respondent Nos.3 to 4.
2.

This Writ Petition is filed seeking a writ of Mandamus to declare the action of the respondents in not depositing the entire decretal amount to the credit of E.P.No.62 of 2022 in L.A.O.P.No.693 of 2011 on the file of the Principal District Judge, Kamareddy are arbitrary and illegal.

3. It is the case of the petitioners herein that the land was acquired by the respondents and an Award by proceedings No.B/2288/07-3 dated 26.10.2009, was passed under Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short, 'the Act, 1894') and aggrieved thereby, the SK,J petitioners herein sought for reference under Section 18 of the Act, 1894, and the same was referred to the Court of the VII Additional District Judge, Bodhan, and the same was taken on the file as L.A.O.P.No.693 of 2011 and finally, the same was disposed of by an order, dated 21.10.2016 enhancing the compensation.

entities.text: Court of the VII Additional District Judge, Bodhan
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Aggrieved thereby, the respondent-State herein filed an appeal before this Court in L.A.A.S.No.158 of 2018 and the same was dismissed by a Division bench of this Court by Judgment, dated 23.09.2022.
In spite of the same, the respondents have not paid compensation amount as enhanced by the reference Court.
Therefore, the petitioners filed E.P.No.62 of 2022 in L.A.O.P.No.693 of 2011 on the file of the Principal District Judge, Kamareddy, seeking execution of the decree passed by the reference Court.
At that stage, the petitioners approached this Court by filing the present Writ Petition seeking a direction to the respondents to deposit the decretal amount into the credit of E.P.No.62 of 2022.
SK,J 4.

Having regard to the above backdrop of the case, this Court is of the considered view that the authorities cannot take their own time to deposit the amounts, which are already enhanced by the competent Court.

The inaction of the respondents in paying the enhanced compensation amounts in time to the petitioners, who are already suffering from the loss of their lands would make them to also suffer untold hardship and misery and run from pillar to post for getting the enhanced compensation deposited and incur expenses for the same.
They will also have to incur additional expenditure for approaching the Court for seeking the required relief.

With the rising inflation, the value of the money will also go down and the delayed payment of the enhanced compensation will result in the compensation amount itself losing all the charm and utility.

If the petitioners or similarly situated persons receive the enhanced compensation within the time, they will be in a position to use that amount in some other investments and get some returns over the same.

Having regard to the same, the Writ Petition is disposed of and the respondent No.5 is directed to deposit the decretal amount in terms of the order and decree, dated 21.10.2016, passed in L.A.O.P.No.693 of 2011 on the file of VII Additional District Judge, Bodhan, to the credit of E.P.No.62 of 2022 in L.A.O.P.No.693 of 2011 on the file of the Principal District Judge, Kamareddy,
as expeditiously as possible, at any rate within a period of four (4) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
There shall be no order as to costs.
6. Miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
There shall be no order as to costs.

JUSTICE K.SARATH Date: 10.01.2024 spk K.Siddiram vs The State Of Telangana on 10 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140574990/
